titles: Why Can't You Tickle Yourself? 🤔 The Brain Trick in 60 Seconds
Your Brain Cancels Your Own Tickles. Here's How
short.description: Try to tickle your own ribs: nothing happens. Your brain keeps a copy of every movement command and predicts exactly what your own touch will feel like, then turns that feeling down. A tickling-robot experiment shows what happens when the prediction is wrong.

titles: Why Can't You Tickle Yourself? The Surprising Science of Tickling
The Brain Trick That Stops You Tickling Yourself
Tickling Explained: Efference Copies, Tickle Robots and Why We're Ticklish
long.description: Why can't you tickle yourself? In this Curious Minds episode we explore the two kinds of tickle (knismesis and gargalesis), what Aristotle, Galileo and Darwin thought, the efference copy your brain keeps of every movement, the 1998 tickling-robot experiment, why a delay makes your own touch tickly again, and the leading ideas about why tickling exists at all.
